title: Exemplar Orchestration Playpen
content:
Purpose:
- Personal scratchpad for experimenting with exemplar orchestration: techniques for dynamically composing few-shot sets, mixing exemplar types (positive/negative/neutral), and lightweight runtime selection heuristics. Goal is to surface brittle patterns and quick mitigation ideas before formalizing into prompt-lib.

Notes-to-self / high-level intuition:
- Treat exemplar bank as a small choreography: role (instruction), exemplar (input/output pair), and cue (why this exemplar matters for target).
- Hypothesis: giving the model a short "why" line after each exemplar (1 sentence) reduces hallucination drift in multi-turn instructions. Needs A/B.
- Keep exemplar diversity: lexical paraphrase + reasoning style + error-example. Negative exemplars (explicitly wrong outputs) help with overconfident hallucination in factual transforms.

Quick experiments (run IDs recorded in GH PR above):
1) concat-why-1 (2026-01-14) — 3 exemplars, each exemplar has: user prompt | reference output | 1-line rationale. Model: open-compat-7B-quant. Result: fewer invented steps in procedural tasks, but slight verbosity increase.
2) anti-exemplar (2026-01-28) — 2 positive exemplars, 1 negative (shows wrong answer and says "don't do this"). Model: hosted-latest. Result: reduces confident wrong assertions ~+18% on small eval set; sometimes model parrots the negative example phrasing.
3) exemplar-order-scan (2026-02-03) — permutations of exemplar order. Observed order sensitivity; put most similar exemplar first reduces top-level structural errors.

Representative exemplar templates (copyable):
- Compact how-to (positive exemplar):
  Q: "Summarize steps to boil an egg for a soft yolk."
  A: "1) Place eggs in pot, cover with cold water. 2) Heat to a simmer, then start timer 6.5 minutes. 3) Transfer to ice bath; peel."
  Why: "Short, numbered steps help the model give concise procedures without adding optional tips."

- Transformation exemplar (neutral):
  Q: "Rewrite the sentence to passive voice: 'The team shipped the build.'"
  A: "The build was shipped by the team."
  Why: "Example shows mapping of active->passive for short sentences; keeps focus on syntactic change."

- Anti-exemplar (negative):
  Q: "Convert currency to USD given exchange rate 0.9 (EUR->USD). Amount: 100 EUR"
  A: "120 USD"
  Why: "Bad math example showing off-by-factor error; included to signal verifier to avoid naive inversions."

Failure cases observed (notes):
- Model sometimes treats the "Why:" lines as part of the output it should produce. Mitigation: separate with explicit delimiter: "---exemplar-end---" or put rationale in parentheses and preface with "(rationale)". Tradeoff: more tokens.
- Negative exemplars occasionally prime the model to repeat the wrong pattern when asked to "explain why that's wrong" — it uses the negative exemplar as an authoritative example. Need to test stronger wording e.g., "Incorrect example (for contrast):" and follow with explicit label "DO NOT REPEAT".
- Order sensitivity: similar exemplars earlier reduce structure errors but increase mimicry of phrasing. If target requires diversity of phrasing, randomize order across requests or implement rotation in runtime.

Small eval snapshot (toy set n=40 procedural prompts):
- base few-shot 3-ex: exact-good-steps: 60%
- +why-lines: exact-good-steps: 73%
- +anti-ex: hallucinated facts reduced by 18% but verbosity +12%
Note: numbers noisy — ran on hosted test window at low qps. Need larger, controlled run.

Runtime orchestration ideas (for prompt-lib):
- exemplars_by_goal(goal_embedding) -> top-k by cosine, then apply filters: lexical-levenshtein to avoid near-duplicates, and apply at-most-one-negative policy.
- rotation-window: keep a ring buffer per user session to avoid repeating same exemplar ordering.
- concise-rationale toggle: if output token budget < X, drop 'Why' lines.
- exemplar-labels: prefix exemplar with [POSITIVE] [NEGATIVE] [NEUTRAL] to reduce confusion. Test cost vs benefit.

Play examples (few-shot sets used in experiments):
- Set A (3 exemplars, concat why):
  1) Q: "Create a 3-step checklist for deploying a static site."
     A: "1) Build site locally. 2) Push to CDN. 3) Verify HTTPS."
     Why: "Checklist style -> concise steps"
  2) Q: "Turn this into a one-line product blurb: 'Fast deploys for docs'"
     A: "Deploy docs in seconds with a single command."
     Why: "Shows compressing copy to marketing tone"
  3) Q: "Convert short instruction to imperative list: 'You should restart the server daily'"
     A: "Restart the server daily to clear memory."
     Why: "Shows imperative rewriting pattern"

- Set B (2 positive + 1 anti):
  Positive1: mapping small math conversions (good example)
  Positive2: passive->active mapping
  Anti: wrong unit conversion (labelled 'incorrect')

Incidental UX ideas (for Console integration):
- Display exemplar provenance (author, created_at) in Console when using prompt-lib so teams understand drift.
- Quick toggle to show/hide 'Why' lines to save tokens in production paths.
- Exemplar-edit diffs: track small changes to exemplars because tiny wording shifts often change model behavior dramatically.

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- Q1: Does labelling negative exemplars as explicitly 'incorrect' avoid mimicry more effectively than prefixing with contextual warning text? (A/B)
- Q2: Is there a diminishing return after 4 exemplars for procedural tasks? Test with n=[1,2,3,4,6].
- Q3: For multi-turn dialog, is it better to interleave exemplars that include multi-turn examples or only single-turn pairs?
- Q4: How much token overhead do 'Why' lines add vs the improvement in hallucination? Build ROI curve.

Quick todo (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Run controlled 1k prompt eval with rotation vs fixed order (Samir to spin up job).
- [ ] Try alternative delimiter experiments: "<Rationale>..." vs "(rationale)" (Lena to run replays).
- [ ] Draft a short Confluence note summarizing positive results + recommended runtime heuristics (goal: product-hosted-api proposal).

Random brainstorm fragments (notes to future self):
- Maybe include a micro-metadata tag per exemplar: "style: terse|explanatory|stepwise" and let runtime prefer style matching the request.
- Could attach a small verifier chain that checks numeric transforms (units/currency) rather than relying solely on exemplars.
- For negative exemplars, try showing the correct answer after the negative example rather than just labelling it. Sequence: Negative example -> "Why it's wrong" -> Correct example.
